title: Infosys' weak Q4 earnings have a price, brokerages slash targets by 9-13%
summary: Infosys posted a 12% year-on-year drop in Q4 net profit and missed revenue estimates. The company forecasted flat to modest revenue growth of 0–3% in constant currency and an operating margin of 20–22% for FY26. Brokerages including Nuvama and Emkay cut FY26-27 EPS and target prices by about 9–13% while retaining buy ratings.
content:
Infosys reported a 12% year-on-year decline in Q4 net profit and missed revenue estimates, prompting a reassessment of near-term expectations among sell-side analysts.

In its guidance the company projected revenue growth of 0%–3% in constant currency for the fiscal year and set an operating margin target in the range of 20%–22% for FY26. The cautious revenue outlook and margin band reflect managements assessment of demand and pricing dynamics in the near term.

Following the results and guidance, brokerages including Nuvama and Emkay cut FY26 and FY27 earnings per share estimates and reduced their target prices by roughly 9% to 13%. Despite trimming forecasts and price targets, several firms maintained buy ratings, citing continued deal wins, a healthy services pipeline and the companys strategic positioning in key technology segments.

Market participants noted that the combination of a weak quarterly performance and conservative forward guidance typically leads to multiple compression until visibility on growth improves. Analysts said they will closely monitor new deal intake, client spend patterns across industries, and execution on cost levers that could support margins.

Investors and observers will also watch macro factors that influence enterprise IT budgets, including interest rate trends and global economic conditions, which can affect demand for digital transformation services. For Infosys, sustaining deal momentum and demonstrating margin resilience will be central to restoring investor confidence.

The broader equity market and technology sector reaction reflected the recalibration of earnings expectations, with brokerages highlighting the need for clearer signs of demand recovery before revising longer term forecasts more aggressively.

Outlook

Near term, analysts expect stock performance to hinge on quarterly delivery, commentary around pipeline health, and managements ability to translate bookings into revenue and operating profit. Continued scrutiny from both domestic and international investors means the companys guidance and subsequent execution will remain in focus over the coming quarters.
